introduction_markdown: Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour and Section II in 1½ hours. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. In Section II answer EITHER parts a, b and c OR parts d, e and f of each question (Section II: answer ALL questions, choosing one question from each pair of alternatives). For your guidance the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Where necessary, assume: the acceleration of free fall, $g = 10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$; the speed of light in air, $c = 3\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the charge on an electron, $e = 1.6\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm{C}$. Calculators are allowed.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Two isotopes of carbon are designated as: $^{12}_{6}\mathrm{C}$ and $^{14}_{6}\mathrm{C}$.

(i) What are isotopes? *[1 mark]*

(ii) Determine the neutron-proton (N/Z) ratio for each of the isotopes and hence deduce which of them is more stable. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Isotopes** are atoms of the same element which have the same number of protons (the same atomic number $Z$) but different numbers of neutrons (different mass numbers $A$).

(ii) Number of neutrons $N = A - Z$.

- $^{12}_{6}\mathrm{C}$: $Z = 6$ protons, $N = 12 - 6 = 6$ neutrons, so $N/Z = \dfrac{6}{6} = 1$.
- $^{14}_{6}\mathrm{C}$: $Z = 6$ protons, $N = 14 - 6 = 8$ neutrons, so $N/Z = \dfrac{8}{6} = 1.33$.

For light nuclei such as carbon, stable nuclei have $N/Z \approx 1$. $^{12}_{6}\mathrm{C}$ has $N/Z = 1$ whereas $^{14}_{6}\mathrm{C}$ has too many neutrons ($N/Z = 1.33$) and is radioactive. Therefore **$^{12}_{6}\mathrm{C}$ is the more stable isotope**.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Explain why an atom is said to be neutral, even though it contains charged particles. *[2 marks]*

(ii) Name the part of an atom where it's mass is mostly concentrated. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) An atom contains positively charged protons in the nucleus and negatively charged electrons around it. The number of protons equals the number of electrons, and a proton and an electron carry equal and opposite charges. The positive and negative charges therefore cancel out, so the atom has no net charge.

(ii) The **nucleus** (protons and neutrons), because electrons have a negligible mass.
